title: 2Sum Problem
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
problemStatement: Given an array and a target, find whether two elements sum to the target (and return their indices).
intuition: Fixing one element turns the problem into "does the complement target - x exist?" — a lookup, not a search. A hash map answers it in O(1); if the array is sorted, two pointers answer it in O(1) space.

approaches.title: Brute: all pairs
Optimal (indices): one-pass hash map
approaches.idea: Look up the complement among elements already seen, then insert x.
approaches.dryRun:
a=[2,6,5,8,11] target=14
i=0 need 12 absent, store 2
i=1 need 8 absent, store 6
i=2 need 9 absent, store 5
i=3 need 6 present -> (1,3)
approaches.whyWorks: Checking before inserting guarantees i != j without any special case.

approaches.title: Optimal (yes/no, sorted input): two pointers
approaches.idea: If the sum is too small move left up, too large move right down.
approaches.time: O(n log n) with the sort, O(n) if already sorted
approaches.whyWorks: Each move discards only pairs that cannot possibly reach the target.

specialTechnique.title: Hash map vs two pointers
specialTechnique.body: Need original indices -> hash map (sorting destroys them). Need O(1) space or the array is already sorted -> two pointers. This fork repeats in 3-Sum, 4-Sum and Two Sum in BST.

commonMistakes: Inserting x before checking its complement, which pairs an element with itself
Sorting when the question asks for original indices
patternRecognition: "Pair with property X" -> complement lookup; sorted variant -> converging pointers
followUps: Return all unique pairs, not just one
What if the array is a stream of unknown length?
How would you handle adversarial hash collisions?
interviewInsight: The expected conversation is brute -> hash -> "what if sorted / O(1) space?". Volunteer both endpoints.
